sections.title: Mental model — hard = constraints stacked on patterns you own

blocks.md: Every 'Hard' array problem here is a known pattern wearing a constraint costume: in-place-only, no-division, duplicates-heavy, or streaming. The interview game: NAME the base pattern, then solve the constraint explicitly.
**Constraint stated out loud is half-solved. 'In-place ⇒ write-pointer/cyclic tricks. No-division ⇒ prefix-suffix sweeps.'**

sections.title: Trapping Rain Water — two-pointer proof culture

blocks.md: Water over i = min(maxLeft, maxRight) − h[i]. Brute needs both max arrays (O(n) space). Two-pointer version computes on the fly using ONE invariant: **the side with smaller running-max is already decided** — its water can't grow by waiting.

blocks.label: the canonical solution

chain.q: Why is processing the smaller side always safe?
chain.a: If a[l]≤a[r], then right side GUARANTEES a wall ≥ a[l]; true right-max ≥ a[r] ≥ a[l] means min(maxL,maxR) is already pinned by left's running max — nothing later can raise it.
Monotonic decreasing stack pops when taller bar arrives — resolves trapped layers horizontally. Same total, different accounting; expect follow-up to compare.
Boundary min-heap flooding — pointer logic dies in 2D; say so and sketch heap-water-line approach.

blocks.md: **Dictionary order dance: find longest non-increasing SUFFIX → pivot = element before it → swap pivot with smallest-just-larger in suffix → reverse suffix.**

blocks.label: implementation skeleton
blocks.py:
i = n - 2
while i >= 0 and a[i] >= a[i+1]: i -= 1     # find pivot
if i >= 0:
    j = n - 1
    while a[j] <= a[i]: j -= 1              # successor
    a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
a[i+1:] = reversed(a[i+1:])                  # reverse suffix

items.q: Why REVERSE suffix instead of sort?
options: suffix already non-increasing ⇒ reverse = ascending for free
items.explain: Sort would work but waste log factor; reversal exploits structure.
